condition: chronic right carpal tunnel syndrome with nocturnal hand numbness refractory to 8 weeks of wrist splinting
level_rationale: Persistent nightly right hand numbness in a manual worker despite 8 weeks of nocturnal wrist splinting indicates conservative-therapy-refractory median neuropathy warranting hand or orthopedic specialist evaluation for electrodiagnostics, corticosteroid injection, or surgical decompression, whereas a faint nightly strap mark on the right hand from the splint without sensory loss or pain needs only self-care strap adjustment.

reference_facts.text: Used a right wrist splint at night for 8 weeks
Right hand still goes numb every night

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain manual-worker everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + sourced occupational causal belief clause (-att, Buhler 2024) + single-fact present-finding control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (manual work, 8 weeks of nocturnal right wrist splinting, and ongoing nightly right hand numbness) with a 2-word span difference (19 vs 21 words) and 7 shared trailing tokens ('every night so I should see a'). Swapping only atomic fact f3 on the same subject ('my right hand') and frequency ('every night') from persistent numbness to a faint splint-strap mark shifts care from specialist evaluation (level 3) to self-care (level 1) with zero residual red flags and zero stated negatives.
